title: TAPA-CS: Enabling Scalable Accelerator Design on Distributed HBM-FPGAs
problem: Existing programming tools cannot effectively partition and compile large accelerator designs across cloud-scale, multi-die FPGA clusters. Developers lack frameworks to leverage distributed fabric, HBM, and on-chip memory while maintaining high frequency and throughput.
motivation: FPGAs are increasingly adopted in compute clouds, but lack of proper compilation frameworks prevents developers from efficiently building high-performance distributed accelerators.
method: TAPA-CS automatically divides large accelerator programs across a cluster of FPGAs with high-bandwidth memory, spreading the workload to prevent bottlenecks and balance resource use. It carefully plans where components should go (floor-planning) and speeds up communication paths within and between FPGAs (through interconnect pipelining) to maintain high-frequency operation. The FPGAs connect through 100Gbps Ethernet, and the system overlaps communication with computation—while data is sent between chips, they simultaneously process other data.
key_novelty: The key innovation is automatically splitting accelerator designs across multiple HBM-FPGAs using layout planning and pipelined communication to enable both scalability and high-frequency operation.
contributions: Open-source framework enabling virtually unlimited accelerator fabric, HBM, and on-chip memory across distributed FPGAs
Automatic design partitioning with congestion control, resource balancing, and communication-computation overlap
Coarse-grained floor-planning coupled with interconnect pipelining for high-frequency operation
